open_claims.claim: The CHANGELOG entry says the spec review found no correction needed and that in `calls` the called MF is smaller than the caller. But `calls` says '17 ve 18 hepsini çağırır', so 17 calls 18 and 18 calls 17, which is a cycle and breaks that ordering rule. The same push files reports/spec-004-calls-17-18.json about this very line, so the review claim contradicts the Founder's own report.

loop.fetch.fetch has no caller in the live path: its own docstring in cek.py says 'nothing calls it yet', and only test_fetch.py runs it. This breaks Y4 (a mechanism with no caller; code with tests but off the live path should leave the live path in the same PR).

The new harness.pass_row module breaks Y4. Its own docstring says 'nothing calls it yet', and status/off_live.json lists it as unwired, so it is a mechanism with tests (T45) but no caller on the live path. Y4 says such code leaves the live path in the same PR. Instead the push adds a new off-live entry and a new test hook for it.

read_map only catches OSError and ValueError, so a deeply nested JSON map file raises an uncaught RecursionError. The spec says an unusable map file must give exit 2 with {ok:false,error}; here it exits 1 with a traceback, which is also the exit code for 'maps differ'.
